scope: Dependency-free shared foundation and portable ingestion preparation; no live engine cutover
approach: Read existing MySQL implementation and planning before changes; reuse mysqlstore, pinned River dependencies and owner coding practices.
Keep shared mechanics separate from owner SQL, authorization and business transitions.
Preserve existing unrelated staged performance-harness and optional-outbox changes.
implemented: Shared typed scalar/text codecs, explicit pool-budget validation, optional pool/transaction observations and reusable owner-ledger/bootstrap mechanics from the preceding foundation pass remain in place.
Extracted bounded data-model maintenance host into generic workers.MaintenanceScheduler with independent cursors and explicit partial/uncertain failure reporting.
Added bounded fair queue probing, immutable optional poll jitter and atomic host metrics; these do not activate handlers or choose deployment concurrency.
Added shared error-history, completion/retry/exhaustion/cancellation/retention policies; data-model MySQL delivery store adopts them without changing tenant/lease fences or atomic owner effects.

Added bounded UTC-microsecond interval occurrence planning for explicit catch-up/coalesce/skip-late policies. Durable schedule rows, unique occurrence insertion and watermark transactions remain owner work.
Added strict fifteen-kind legacy export validation and explicit ingestion-v1 identity decoding; no inferred tenants, fabricated error histories or running-work replay. This is not a target importer.
Data-model metadata transaction manager supports optional shared observations without moving authorization outside its transaction.
Ingestion domain ports/services no longer expose pgx transactions or depend on River. Typed transaction-bound enqueue/retry methods replace RawTx; AST boundary tests guard imports.
Removed ingestion success-through-noop producers and non-atomic creation fallbacks. Client construction errors propagate; actual API/worker producers are wired to the owner transaction.

Ingestion retries use version-1 per-domain-attempt delivery identity, preserving River required uniqueness states while preventing a retained/running earlier attempt from swallowing retries. Legacy v0 remains accepted.

Ingestion API/worker startup and API readiness verify pinned public River lineage, objects, columns, index and required role access; connectivity alone is insufficient. Validation never installs or repairs schema.
Data-model, ingestion and decision metadata-down commands preserve shared River objects; River-down calls reject before connecting.
Added isolated PostgreSQL ingestion fixture and per-test generated disposable databases; fixed test-only concurrent Gin global-mode writes discovered by the race detector.
Updated shared and ingestion checklists to distinguish implemented helpers/adoption from remaining owner contracts and full-system acceptance.
